title: Prove the sharp rank cost for a fixed binary stage factor
body:
## Summary

Scoped proof over F₂, produced by Nick Petalas. Fix an `n × n` first factor `A` in the ordered identity `(I+xA)(I+xB)(I+xC)=(1+x)I`. Prescribe the multiplicities `b,c` of `1+x` in the companion determinants. A completion exists exactly when `A³=A²` and `b,c` are nonnegative integers with `b+c=n-rank(A²)`. If `r=rank(A+A²)`, the minimum ordinary rank sum is

```text
n + r + max(0,r-b) + max(0,r-c)
```

The lower bound comes from `BC=A+A²`. Explicit blocks attain both companion rank bounds together. The shared two-dimensional block comes from unpaidmoon's #7027 at `1ba2ac5adfe58fbe9dba34d50d4e5d30633ce3d0`. Credit aliromman for the paired-star setting in #5747 and the idempotent-leading classification in #7706 at `79ff656972d66915977e816b23ffdcef42fb0e12`.

The `joint-query-controller` card changes scope to the algebraic rank requirement for this stage. Canonical base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`. [Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19717648).

## Evidence

The earlier example gives one non-idempotent first factor with a completion. The proof gives the exact minimum for every fixed first factor and admissible split. The replay explicitly multiplies all 232,576 candidate pairs with non-idempotent first factors through dimension three, finds minima in 345 feasible valuation fibers, and checks 930 attaining block witnesses through dimension ten. Reversing one companion pair is rejected.

From the repository root with CPython 3.12.15 and the standard library:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/paired-star-factor-rank
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/paired-star-factor-rank --check-source-history
python3.12 -I -B -W error -X dev research/paired-star-factor-rank/verify.py
python3.12 -I -O -B -W error -X dev research/paired-star-factor-rank/verify.py
```

Both registered modes pass locally in 0.90 seconds each and print `PASS_PAIRED_STAR_FACTOR_RANK pairs=232576 fibers=345 witnesses=930 controls=1`. Committed bytes and source history also pass.

The proof covers the formal stage and ordinary rank. Native frames, owned storage, restoration, the full signed caller invoice and any κ improvement remain open. The full selected replay, native and Lean replays, independent human review and formal proof-kernel review were unrun.

## Open next questions

- Realize one attaining shared block on a named stage and charge its basis change and restoration.
- Determine the attainable even valuation splits when all three factors must commute with the stage operator `T`.

## Related open work

- #7027 exhibits the non-idempotent first factor and the shared block used here.
- #7706 classifies and counts all middle factors after an idempotent first factor.
- #7040 classifies the idempotent companions of one fixed rank-one stage factor.
- #7223 classifies the middle matrices of that fixed rank-one stage factor.
- #7039 studies one square-zero insertion beside a diagonal stage factor.
- #7103 studies two constant square-zero insertions in the diagonal stage word.
- #7191 studies polynomial entries at those two insertion gaps.
- #7222 studies a square-zero insertion beside the non-idempotent #7027 factor.
